OPENS Ch 5 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR (per source-fidelity note: this entry frames the chapter's likely theological-content based on homiletic-anthology genre-expectation + the Ch 4-→-natural-development trajectory). Ch 5 likely develops CHARITY AND MERCY as the virtue-catalog following complete-repentance (seed 4:34). The charity-and-mercy theme parallels: MATTHEW 5:7 ('Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy'); MATTHEW 25:31-46 (the sheep-and-goats judgment by acts of mercy); LUKE 10:25-37 (the Good Samaritan); JAMES 2:13 ('mercy rejoiceth against judgment'); 1 JOHN 3:17-18 (love-in-deed-and-in-truth); TOBIT 4:7-11 (the canonical-EOTC charity catechism); SIRACH 3:30 ('water will quench a flaming fire; and alms maketh an atonement for sins'). The Tewahedo monastic-tradition preserves the charity-and-mercy chapter as one of the SEVEN-FOLD VIRTUE catalogs that structure the spiritual-formation pedagogy.

HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of ALMSGIVING theme. The almsgiving-theme parallels: MATTHEW 6:1-4 (the manner-of-almsgiving — secret + not-trumpeted); TOBIT 12:8-9 ('it is better to give alms than to lay up gold... alms doth deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin'); ACTS 9:36 + 10:1-4 (Tabitha + Cornelius examples — almsgiving + prayer the canonical-paired-virtues); 2 CORINTHIANS 9:6-15 (Pauline cheerful-giver almsgiving theology); CYPRIAN De Opere et Eleemosynis (the foundational Latin patristic almsgiving-treatise); JOHN CHRYSOSTOM Homilies on Matthew 52 + 78 (the most extended Greek patristic almsgiving exhortation). The Tewahedo Sǝnkǝsar (Synaxarium) preserves almsgiving as one of the CORE-SEVEN-CHARITIES (feed-hungry + give-drink + clothe-naked + visit-sick + visit-imprisoned + house-stranger + bury-dead — the seven-fold-corporal-works-of-mercy preserved in Tewahedo catechesis).
